security_audit.summary: Most command and network findings are Markdown, comments, fixed CLI checks, or temporary-file handling. The confirmed risk is intentional access to hidden Codex session rollout files, plus a semantic risk where concurrent Codex sessions could be mixed into extraction. No evidence found of prompt injection attempts or unauthorized third-party exfiltration in the reviewed files.

content.user_title: Generate GPT Image 2 Assets with Codex
content.value_statement: Teams need fast image generation without separate image API accounts. This skill routes explicit GPT Image 2 requests through Codex CLI and an existing ChatGPT plan.
actual_capabilities: Generates images from text prompts through the Codex CLI imagegen tool.
Edits or restyles images using one or more local reference files.
Supports multi-reference composition by passing each reference image to Codex.
Extracts generated image payloads from new Codex session rollout files.
Writes PNG, JPEG, JPG, or WebP files to the requested output path.
limitations: Requires Codex CLI, a local login, and a ChatGPT plan with image generation access.
Does not provide direct OpenAI API access or a separate billing path.
Reads new Codex session rollout files under the local home directory.
Concurrent Codex sessions can make image extraction ambiguous.

use_cases.title: Create Concept Art
use_cases.description: Designers can turn short briefs into image drafts while staying inside Claude Code or Codex.

use_cases.title: Restyle Brand Assets
use_cases.description: Marketing teams can apply a new style to approved reference images.

use_cases.title: Prototype App Visuals
use_cases.description: Developers can generate placeholders, icons, and mock product images during implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use GPT Image 2 to create a square image of [subject] in [style]. Save it as [file name].

prompt_templates.title: Edit a Reference Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use GPT Image 2 with the attached reference. Keep the main composition, but change [specific elements] to [new direction].

prompt_templates.title: Create a Style Variant
prompt_templates.prompt: Use GPT Image 2 to make three visual directions for [asset]. Keep [brand constraints] and vary lighting, palette, and layout.

prompt_templates.title: Compose Multiple References
prompt_templates.prompt: Use GPT Image 2 with these references. Combine the subject from image one, the color system from image two, and the layout from image three.

output_examples.input: Use GPT Image 2 to create a poster for a product launch in a minimal editorial style.
output_examples.output: A finished poster image is saved to the requested file path, ready for review or iteration.

output_examples.input: Use this logo reference and repaint it as a vintage travel sticker.
output_examples.output: A restyled image keeps the original logo shape while changing texture, color, and presentation.

output_examples.input: Create a product mockup from these two references.
output: A generated product mockup combines the selected subject and style cues.
The assistant reports the saved image location after extraction succeeds.

best_practices: Use this skill only when the user explicitly asks for GPT Image 2 or ChatGPT Images 2.0.
Provide clear output paths and keep reference images in accessible local locations.
Review generated images before publishing, especially when prompts include text or logos.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill as a silent fallback for general image requests.
Do not pass confidential reference images unless the user accepts Codex and ChatGPT processing.
Do not run it during other Codex image sessions when exact session separation matters.

faq.question: Does this skill include image generation access?
faq.answer: No. It requires an existing ChatGPT plan and a working Codex CLI login.

faq.question: Can it edit existing images?
faq.answer: Yes. The script accepts one or more local reference images for restyling or image-to-image edits.

faq.question: Does it call the OpenAI API directly?
faq.answer: No. It uses Codex CLI and the user's existing logged-in ChatGPT session.

faq.question: Where are images saved?
faq.answer: The caller chooses the output path. The extractor only allows PNG, JPEG, JPG, or WebP extensions.

faq.question: Why does it read Codex session files?
faq.answer: Codex stores image payloads in new rollout files. The script extracts the generated image from those files.

faq.question: Can it work without Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can run through Codex-compatible workflows, but the skill instructions target Claude Code and Codex.
